covers: Wall Street close and oil settlement on Fri 23 Oct (to 22:15 SAST); earlier JSE, Europe, US data and company items kept from the 21:15 update
headline: Wall Street closes lower: Dow −1.2%, S&P 500 −0.5% as Brent settles at $116.72, a six-month high; SA unveils plan to run offshore money from home
summary: The rand was at about R16.51/$ in the afternoon, roughly 0.2% weaker on the day (Trading Economics, 23 Oct), and the Reserve Bank, Treasury and JSE briefed investors on a draft framework that lets licensed funds managed from South Africa hold up to 100% foreign assets (Sunday World, 23 Oct). On Wall Street the Dow closed down 652.82 points (−1.23%) at 52,215.16, the S&P 500 fell 0.52% to 7,623.68 and the Nasdaq 0.21% to 25,955.34; the S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell for a second week while the Dow ended the week higher (Yahoo Finance, 23 Oct). Brent settled at $116.72 a barrel, a six-month high and a third weekly gain, with WTI just above $103, on Middle East supply fears (Yahoo Finance, 23 Oct) — a fuel-price and inflation risk for South Africa.

items.title: Wall Street close: Dow −1.23%, S&P 500 −0.52%, Nasdaq −0.21%
items.summary: On Fri 23 Oct the Dow closed at 52,215.16 (−652.82, −1.23%), the S&P 500 at 7,623.68 (−39.75, −0.52%), the Nasdaq Composite at 25,955.34 (−53.52, −0.21%) and the Russell 2000 at 2,775.84 (−0.29%). The S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell for a second straight week; the Dow still ended the week higher (TheStreet puts its weekly gain at about 1.4%). Airlines United, Delta and American each fell more than 4% on fuel costs, American Express fell 3% after announcing about 5% job cuts, while Palo Alto Networks (+7.2%) and Cloudflare (+7.3%) led cybersecurity higher. The 10-year Treasury yield was about 4.99% and the VIX 19.72 (Yahoo Finance, 23 Oct).

items.title: Brent settles at $116.72, a six-month high and third weekly gain; WTI just above $103
items.summary: Brent for December delivery settled at $116.72 a barrel on Fri 23 Oct, its highest in six months and a third straight weekly gain; WTI closed just above $103 (quoted at $103.56, +4.1%) (Yahoo Finance, 23 Oct). Intraday Brent reached $117.26 (Business Today). Drivers: President Trump said the US was not negotiating with Iran, a drone attack on Saudi Arabia's Shaybah oil field was reported, and markets are watching the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. For South Africa this adds to fuel-price and inflation pressure. Gold ended near $4,011 (−1.2%).

items.title: Deckers (DECK) about −8% pre-market at $78.60; Piper Sandler cuts to Underweight, target $75
items.summary: Piper Sandler downgraded Deckers to Underweight from Neutral on Fri 23 Oct and cut its price target to $75 from $100, calling the Q2 sales miss the first in at least five years and saying HOKA and UGG are showing signs of maturity (UGG direct-to-consumer sales −8%) (Investing.com). Needham kept a Buy but cut its target to $96 from $125; the shares were down 7.8% at $78.60 pre-market (Benzinga, 23 Oct). This follows Q2 revenue of $1.48bn versus about $1.51bn expected and a full-year sales outlook cut to $5.700–5.725bn. DECK is a BUY on our list with a 6-month target of $103; $78.60 is below the watchlist pullback entry (88.10) and stop (82.94), so the rating needs an analyst re-run with the new guidance — the rating is unchanged. In early US trading on Friday DECK was down 8.38% (TheStreet). TheStreet's live page later showed DECK down 6.17% at 10:14 ET (16:14 SAST).

items.title: Final October consumer sentiment 48; inflation expectations edge up
items.summary: The University of Michigan's final October sentiment index was 48, above the 46.3 consensus (the preliminary reading) and little changed from 48.1 in September. One-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7% from 4.6% and long-run expectations to 3.5% from 3.4% (released 10:00 ET / 16:00 SAST, Fri 23 Oct). Spot gold was at $4,014.71/oz (+0.24%) shortly after.

items.title: US flash PMIs: services slow to 57.9, manufacturing 56.0
items.summary: S&P Global's October flash services PMI was 57.9 versus 58.0 expected and 59.8 in September; manufacturing was 56.0 versus 55.5 expected and 57.0 prior; the composite eased to 57.6 from 58.4 (released 09:45 ET / 15:45 SAST, Fri 23 Oct). Readings above 50 still mean growth.

items.title: Movers: Moderna slides again, Verizon −4.6%, SpaceX rebounds
items.summary: Moderna plunged almost 20% on Thursday and fell another 4% early Friday; Verizon was −4.6% after reports SpaceX may buy cell towers; SpaceX rose 2.4% after a 9% drop on Thursday; American Express was −1.2% despite beating estimates; memory-chip names SK Hynix, Sandisk and Micron rose (early Fri 23 Oct).

items.title: Early movers: American Express −2.85% on job cuts; RingCentral +15%
items.summary: In early trading on Fri 23 Oct American Express fell 2.85% after announcing plans to cut about 5% of its workforce; Deckers was −8.38%, while RingCentral rose 14.95%, Crown Castle 9.83% and Robert Half 8.81%. Gold futures were −0.55% at $4,037.90/oz, silver −1.89% at $53.97 and bitcoin near $81,601.

items.title: Investors buy bonds: US 10-year yield down 16bp to 4.97%
items.summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield fell 16 basis points to 4.97% on Thursday 22 Oct, from 5.13%, having traded above 5.30% earlier in October, as investors moved into bonds during the AI-led stock sell-off. In Europe on Friday, France's 10-year yield was about 5.07% versus Germany's 3.33%, a spread above 170bp.

items.title: Nasdaq −2.6%, S&P 500 −1.2% as AI-trade worries hit tech
items.summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,663.43 and the Nasdaq at 26,008.86; the Dow edged up 0.02% to 52,867.98. Lam Research fell about 9%, Applied Materials and KLA about 6%, AMD and Intel 4–5% and NVIDIA about 2%. Treasuries rallied: the 10-year yield fell about 11bp to near 5.0%.

items.title: Tesla beats, shares still fall 3%
items.summary: Adjusted EPS of $0.48 beat the $0.44 expected and adjusted EBITDA came in at $3.90bn, but revenue of $28.05bn was slightly short and investors weighed higher 2027–28 spending plans.

items.title: Blackstone +8% on exit outlook; jobless claims at a three-month low
items.summary: Blackstone rose 8.4% on an upbeat outlook for exits and fees despite weaker Q3 realisations. Initial jobless claims fell to 194,000.

items.title: Asia slides as the chip rout spreads: Kospi −2.2%, Nikkei −1.4%
items.summary: On Friday 23 Oct the Kospi fell 2.2%, the Kosdaq 3.5%, the Nikkei 1.4% and Shanghai 1.3%, while the Hang Seng edged up 0.25%, after the Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped 6.7% on Thursday. Japan's September core CPI rose to 2.1% y/y (in line, up from 1.7%); the yen firmed to about 156.25 per dollar before easing to 157.

items.title: Europe lower: Stoxx 600 −0.4%, Kering −11% on Gucci sales
items.summary: Early on Fri 23 Oct (about 09:45 SAST) the Stoxx 600 was −0.4%, FTSE 100 −0.3%, DAX −0.5% and CAC 40 −0.8%. Kering fell more than 11% after Gucci's third-quarter sales dropped 6% year on year on a comparable basis, slightly worse than expected.

items.title: SARB, Treasury and JSE outline plan to manage offshore money from South Africa
items.summary: At a briefing on Fri 23 Oct the Reserve Bank, National Treasury and the JSE explained a draft 'Synthetic Financial Centre' framework (published Wednesday 21 Oct). Licensed asset managers, banks, insurers and private-equity firms could run global portfolios in any currency from South Africa, and qualifying vehicles could hold 100% foreign assets. The 45% offshore limit still applies when a local institution commits money to such a vehicle, and the SARB said the 45% limit stays a 'long-term feature'. South African portfolios hold close to R5 trillion offshore; the JSE estimates the framework could attract R10 trillion over time. Comments close 30 November; a second phase may cover tax and foreign-currency listings on local exchanges.

items.title: Rand near R16.51/$, slightly weaker; 2035 bond flat at 8.615%
items.summary: The rand traded at R16.5050/$ at 08:36 SAST on Fri 23 Oct, broadly unchanged from Thursday's close after a sharp fall that session. The 2035 government bond was flat, yielding 8.615%. Traders are waiting for month-end data; better-than-expected inflation and two months of temporary fuel-levy relief are in the background. Later in the day Trading Economics showed USD/ZAR at about 16.51, the dollar up about 0.2% against the rand on 23 Oct.

items.title: Mid-year budget: temporary fuel levy cuts return from November
items.summary: Wednesday's medium-term budget review reintroduced temporary fuel levy relief for two months from November, worth about R10bn, to ease cost-of-living pressure. The 2035 government bond yield was little changed at about 8.6%.

items.title: Gold below $4,000 for the first time since July
items.summary: Spot gold fell 0.3% to $4,013.91 by 03:26 SAST on 23 Oct after slipping 2.8% on Thursday, touching its lowest since 20 July, and is heading for a weekly loss of more than 3.5%; it briefly traded under $4,000. Platinum was flat at $1,567.10 after a 3.6% drop on Thursday. CME FedWatch shows a 78% chance of a December rate hike; the Fed is expected to hold on 27–28 Oct. On Friday morning Trading Economics showed gold near $4,014/oz, down 0.3% on the day and about 6% lower over the past month. Gold futures were −0.8% at $4,027.40/oz around 10:00 SAST on Fri 23 Oct (Euronews).

items.title: Bitcoin below $82,000
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 4% to roughly $81,350 alongside the tech sell-off.

items.title: META −7% after results — on our list as a low-conviction SELL
items.summary: Meta fell 6.98% to $648.85 as investors weighed its quarterly results and a 2-for-1 stock split. Our 14 Oct work-sheet had a 6-month value near $677; at $649 the shares are now below it, so the rating needs a re-run with the new results. On Friday Meta fell about another 2% in midday trade (Upstox, 23 Oct). Separately, a New Mexico judge on Wed 21 Oct ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for misleading Facebook users about data privacy; Meta says it is confident it will win on appeal (Axios). Rating unchanged; re-run pending.

items.title: Chip sell-off: AMD and NVIDIA lower
items.summary: AMD fell more than 8% and NVIDIA 4.4% on Thu 22 Oct; both edged up pre-market on Friday (AMD +~1%, NVIDIA +0.4% at 12:00 SAST, Stocktwits). AMD is a SELL on our list; this morning's watchlist (23 Oct, 06:30) has it as a cleared short setup at 501.59 (stop 558.05), with results within 14 days. NVIDIA is a BUY but is not technically cleared; its pullback entry is 222.63 (stop 210.13). Check both levels at the US open.

items.title: Wabtec beats and lifts profit guidance; shares near $273, still above our SELL value
items.summary: Wabtec's third-quarter sales rose 8.1% to $3.12 billion and adjusted earnings per share rose 22% to $2.83; the 12-month backlog grew 8.8% to $8.99 billion, and the company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS range to $10.85–$11.05 while keeping sales guidance at $12.3–$12.6 billion (Wabtec 8-K, 21 Oct). The shares were at $272.85, down 1.3%, in Friday afternoon trade (StockAnalysis, 23 Oct 15:12 EDT). Our 14 Oct work-sheet has a 6-month value of $248.07; the price is about 10% above it and just above the $271.62 short-setup level on our watchlist. Stronger guidance cuts against the SELL case, so it should be checked at the next re-price. Rating unchanged.
